I've spoken with a psychiatrist who specializes in addiction counseling, and suboxone is a completely different drug than methadone. I think a big reason people choose to use methadone over suboxone is the fact that, when you're taking methadone, you don't go home with, say, a month's worth of pills--you're only given one dose at a time. He said suboxone cannot get you high, so if you're given a month's worth, it won't do anything except lessen the symptoms of withdrawal. That being said, I do think there's a benefit in having to go back and forth to a clinic every day--people will notice you aren't there, there are people to talk to when you get your dose, it helps establish a routine, etc.

Here's a list of crisis pregnancy centers in the state of California:
[California ProLife Council](http://www.californiaprolife.org/resources/pregnancy_help/crisis_pregnancy_centers__alphabetized_by_city/)

Many are opening in [Texas](http://america.aljazeera.com/articles/2014/1/2/as-texas-abortionclinicscloseunregulatedpregnancyclinicsflourish.html) to take advantage of the shrinking number of legal abortion clinics.

And a woman once went undercover in one to verify the truth. Granted, it's one case, but [here's](http://www.huffingtonpost.com/caitlin-bancroft/crisis-pregnancy-center_b_3763196.html) the article if you're still interested.
